newsitem.title: UK: OFT looks at P&O proposed buy of ferry assets.
newsitem.headline: OFT looks at P&O proposed buy of ferry assets.

text.p: UK competition watchdog, the Office of Fair Trading, said on Friday it would be considering whether the proposed acquisition by P&O of a 50 percent stake in North Sea Ferries would qualify for further investigation.
P&O Steam Navigation Company (P&O) has said it is loking to buy the stake from Royal Nedlloyd NV.

If the deal does qualify for investigation under the merger section of the Fair Trading Act, the OFT will look at it with a view to advising the Department of Trade and Industry on whether there should be a referral to the Monopolies and Mergers Commission.
The OFT has invited views on the implications of the deal for competition.
P&O has signed a memorandum of understanding with Royal Nedlloyd to buy the stake for 25.25 million stg, which will give it full control of NSF.
The UK shipping group said the acquisition could result in savings of five million stg per annum for the NSF and Felixstowe and England operations.
The deal, which will result in 100 job cuts, is already due to be examined by the European Commission, competition commissioner Karel van Miert said this week.
